items.summary: Malaria early-warning systems that treat climate as a spatially uniform forcing mis-time vector-control deployment when the thermal niche of Anopheles vectors shifts across districts. The framework is formalised as a structural causal model over a district-month lattice, with a graph-identification condition and a lag-recovery theorem that bounds timing error by the spectral gap of the estimated adjacency matrix. A climate-analytics evaluation is conducted on NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E), 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 °C and a standard deviation of 1.043 °C; the estimated linear trend was −0.1564 °C per decade. The evaluation shows that a causal graph that admits lagged hydrological mediators recovers the intervention window with lower timing error than a temperature-only baseline, and that the error bound tightens as the spectral gap widens. The contribution is a formal link between causal-graph identifiability and the operational quantity that public-health managers actually care about: how many weeks early or late a spraying or net-distribution campaign is triggered.

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-five entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the wave-induced light fluctuations measured by Darecki et al. (2011) and Gernez & Antoine (2009), read from their figures, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.

items.summary: HIMS-CDI Synthetic Data Archive Companion to: "HIMS-CDI: A Governance Specification and Assurance Architecture for CTI-Driven Cybersecurity Risk Assessment in Healthcare" This archive contains the production synthetic-data pipeline, the prespecified correlation matrix, and the labelled 240-environment dataset used in the Phase I specification-validation study reported in Section 4 of the manuscript. The synthetic corpus comprises 240 healthcare cybersecurity environments, each characterised by 20 indicators across five groups (CTI Modality, Semantic Enrichment, Fusion Strategy, Regulatory Traceability, Explainability). The pipeline applies empirical marginal transformations (beta, categorical), generates labels via the three non-compensatory governance gates (CDI ≥ 0.70, CCR ≥ 0.80, latency < 200 ms, memory < 100 MB), injects Gaussian noise (σ = 0.13), and performs a stratified 60/20/20 split (seed 123). The test split yields exactly 48 environments (32 NOT_DEPLOY_SYNTH, 16 DEPLOY_SYNTH), matching the manuscript's specification. Random seeds: 42 = corpus generation; 123 = stratified split; 10-seed sweep = model-training runs. Provenance: The correlation matrix is a prespecified design parameter, not an empirical estimate. MITRE ATT&CK v14.1 technique frequencies and dwell-time parameters (mean 62 days, SD 28 days) are prespecified simulation assumptions, not observed healthcare incident statistics. Epistemic boundary: This archive supports Phase I specification testing only. It does not contain real healthcare incident data, and the synthetic evaluation does not establish clinical safety, operational effectiveness, real-world predictive validity, or operational deployment readiness. Phase II validation against real healthcare incident outcomes is planned (see manuscript Section 6.2–6.3).

items.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are increasingly proposed for downscaling convective-permitting rainfall extremes, yet their behaviour under sparse radiosonde initialization remains poorly characterised for dam-safety analytics, where the upper tail of the rainfall distribution governs spillway design. We define the tail-index distortion functional, derive a bound on its bias under sparse initialization, and show that the distortion is governed by the interaction between the PINN's physics residual weighting and the effective sample size of the initial-condition ensemble. The framework is illustrated with a reanalysis-based temperature series for Lagos, Nigeria (2000–2023; 312 monthly observations; mean 26.414 °C; warming trend 0.1553 °C per decade), which serves as a benchmark for the data-provenance and uncertainty-reporting protocol that dam-safety analytics requires. Tail-index distortion should be treated as a first-class evaluation metric alongside predictive accuracy, and it identifies the conditions under which sparse radiosonde initialization produces non-conservative design quantiles. The contribution is a methodological and conceptual apparatus for auditing PINN downscaling in safety-critical climate analytics, not an empirical validation of any particular PINN architecture.

items.summary: Virtualization-based obfuscation and Mixed Boolean-Arithmetic (MBA) represent the modern standard for software intellectual property concealment and malware defense evasion, transforming native machine instructions into pseudo-random bytecodes executed by an embedded interpreter. Existing deobfuscation paradigms remain fundamentally brittle: dynamic execution tracing achieves incomplete path coverage while triggering anti-analysis defenses; classical Dynamic Symbolic Execution (DSE) suffers from catastrophic path explosion and prohibitive SMT solver latency over modular bit-vector arithmetic; and virtual stack mechanics leave hundreds of dead operations that overwhelm industry decompilers. In this paper, we present AETHER-64, a fully automated, static bytecode-driven devirtualization and algebraic simplification framework engineered specifically for 64-bit protected binaries. AETHER-64 introduces three foundational innovations: (1) Local-Context Handler Symbolic Slicing, which reconstructs complete Control-Flow Graphs (CFGs) through isolated basic block emulation without accumulating global path constraints; (2) a bit-parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction (APR) filter grounded in Boolean conjunction lattice signatures and fast Moebius inversion over Z/2^64, resolving invariant dispatch conditions in O(1) time; and (3) syntax-directed I/O-guided non-linear MBA synthesis coupled with LLVM Static Single Assignment (SSA) virtual stack elimination. We evaluate AETHER-64 on the Quarkslab Diffing Obfuscation Dataset (104 ground-truth functions across MiniLua, Zlib, and SQLite comprising 56,883 bytecode instructions), 1,000 synthetic Tigress virtual machines, commercial protections (VMProtect 3.4/3.5, Themida 3.1), and 7-layer non-linear MBA expressions. AETHER-64 achieves 100% CFG recovery, resolves 93.91% of branch queries via APR filtering with an empirical 2,072.8x speedup over raw SMT resolution, eliminates 91.8% of instruction bloat, and reconstructs clean, human-verifiable C pseudocode with mathematical bisimulation guarantees.
items.title: AETHER-64: High-Throughput Binary Devirtualization via Bit-Parallel Algebraic Pre-Reduction and SSA Bytecode Promotion

items.summary: This protocol presents a systematic, deterministic translation framework for Beinecke MS 408 (The Voynich Manuscript). The framework interprets the manuscript as a 15th-century reverse-indexed chemical and pharmaceutical register produced within an Alpine/Central European workshop tradition. By operating on a phonetic-Latin reconstruction model, the cipher maps Extensible Alphabet Code (EVA) glyphs to a rigid, cross-sectional technical vocabulary. The validity of this protocol is verified through a 4-stage empirical pipeline featuring dual botanical cross-validation (Dragon's Blood resin vs. Opium Poppy latex) and external vernacular anchor verification via the marginalia on Folio 116v.

items.summary: This paper consolidates the Phase and Electromagnetic Coupling programme through twenty-one computational checkpoints, examining connections between phase organisation, electromagnetic response, gravitational sourcing, and optical receiver records within explicitly specified physical models. The analysis connects amplitude and relative phase to internal-state geometry, collective quantum electromagnetic responses, material currents, and the complete stress–energy tensor of a relativistic scalar field. It distinguishes the information contained in a joint source state from the information accessible through a particular coupling, including collective bright and dark responses that cannot be recovered from separate local states alone. In the gravitational calculations, two internal phase arrangements with matching initial local current, stress, and geometry subsequently produce different neutral-probe tidal responses. A specified optical construction carries a selected difference into receiver-clock intervals, radar distance, and interference signals. The response persists in an independently solved zero-charge family, demonstrating that an electromagnetic source field is not required for this particular modelled gravitational phase dependence. The paper also establishes a restricted mathematical connection between the programme’s nested gravitational source proposal and conventional field stress. An amplitude-weighted cosine expression appears as the equal-amplitude, single-component limit of a squared transported field difference. Retaining amplitude variation, internal-state overlap, and directional and temporal information permits reconstruction of the complete source and its gravitational accounting. Foundational Phase remains nonspatial in the proposed interpretation; coordinates and dynamics belong to the represented coupling description. The results are conditional mathematical correspondences and numerical findings using supplied interactions, Maxwell equations, Einstein gravity, and ideal receiver laws. Physical source identification, dimensional calibration, and measured receiver response remain open. The quantum and classical calculations are separate models, with no quantum-to-classical derivation claimed. The accompanying reproducibility release contains the synthesis, branch master, twenty-one checkpoint reports, original computational packages, and a catalogue linking results to their verification procedures.

items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. With audit --apply-repair, GradLint can write corrected FSL bvec/bval files and, optionally, an MRtrix .b table, together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs. WARN decisions additionally require --force-repair. Without --apply-repair, nonidentity corrections are withheld with an overall WARN and exit code 3. GradLint does not verify volume-to-gradient pairing. The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.7, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-23. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. items.summary: Motivation: Variant calling for next-generation sequencing (NGS) data relies on a diverse ecosystem of tools and workflows. Large-scale collaborative studies increasingly adopt federated analysis, where each institution processes sensitive data locally using standardized pipelines. Deploying identical pipelines across multiple centers remains challenging because heterogeneous software environments and computing policies can cause workflow divergence and inconsistent results. Results: We developed CBIcall, a workflow backend-flexible, configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling pipelines from raw FASTQ files to analysis-ready VCFs. Users define each analysis in a single YAML parameters file, which CBIcall resolves against a controlled workflow registry and resource catalog. The execution driver validates parameters and checks compatibility among pipelines, analysis modes, workflow backends, genome builds, tool versions, and resource bundles. CBIcall supports reproducibility auditing by comparing executions using recorded provenance and output fingerprints. CBIcall dispatches validated workflows natively through Bash, Cromwell, Nextflow and Snakemake backends and provides production-ready pipelines for germline WES, WGS (single-sample or cohort joint genotyping following GATK Best Practices), and mitochondrial DNA analysis. We evaluated analytical performance using public benchmark datasets and validated reproducibility across four computing environments. We further deployed CBIcall in the EU HEREDITARY project, where it processed 1102 samples with both WES and mtDNA pipelines on an institutional HPC system, supporting its suitability for reproducible cohort-scale genomic analyses. Availability and implementation: CBIcall is open source (GPLv3) and distributed with ready-to-run pipelines; full dependency and installation documentation is available at https://github.com/CNAG-Biomedical-Informatics/cbicall.

items.summary: HBB2OBB converts horizontal (axis-aligned) bounding boxes (HBBs) into oriented (rotated) bounding boxes (OBBs) by using existing HBB annotations as prompts for segmentation models from the SAM (Segment Anything Model) family. It targets object detection tasks where objects appear at arbitrary orientations, such as aerial imagery, satellite data, and traffic monitoring, producing oriented boxes that tightly encapsulate non-upright objects without any re-annotation. Beyond conversion, it provides horizontal box detection, evaluation, hyperparameter optimization, an interactive annotation viewer, and annotation format-conversion tools, exposed through both a command-line interface and a Python API. 📖 Documentation: rfonod.github.io/hbb2obb , with a quick start on the bundled sample data, a guide per command, pages on how the conversion works, the confidence score, the metrics and provenance, and a CLI and API reference generated from the code. Why HBB2OBB 🎯 Accurate OBBs from HBBs : prompts SAM-family segmentation models with existing horizontal boxes to fit tight oriented boxes around non-upright objects, with no re-annotation required. 🚗 No HBBs? Detect them : the hbb2obb-detect command runs an Ultralytics detector over the images and writes the horizontal boxes the conversion consumes, confidence column included. 🧩 Model ensemble : combines masks from multiple SAM variants through majority voting for more robust, accurate results. 🛡️ Spatially constrained and safe : region-specific masking and contour refinement keep segmentation inside the object, a mask split by an occluder is fitted back together, and a fallback retains the original HBB when no valid mask is found, counted and reported rather than left to be discovered afterwards. 🔎 Confidence-scored output : every OBB receives a heuristic quality score in [0, 1] that flags silent fallbacks and low-confidence conversions, so you know which boxes to trust; the scores go in the label files or in a side-car directory that keeps them strictly standard, and the detector's own confidence can be carried through instead of, or on top of, that score. 📐 Flexible scaling : positive or negative scale factors, optionally different for the short and long sides, recover cropped object parts or tighten overly conservative annotations. 📊 Evaluate and optimize : evaluation against ground truth on IoU, orientation error, and the share of boxes above a high IoU bar, plus the hbb2obb-optimize command, a hyperparameter search over SAM inference resolution, scale factors, and morphological opening kernel, driven by a configuration file so that a whole benchmark of model ensembles is a single reproducible command. 🔬 Where the score comes from : the hbb2obb-analyze command breaks one evaluation down by the ground truth's orientation, size, frame edge, difficulty and class, and scores the conversion against emitting the horizontal prompt unchanged. 🔄 Five annotation formats : read and write YOLO, DOTA, Pascal VOC, COCO, and LabelMe, for horizontal and oriented boxes alike, with a check that proves every format encodes the same boxes. 🔍 Interactive viewer : the hbb2obb-view command pans and zooms over the annotations, in any format, coloring boxes by confidence and overlaying predictions against ground truth. Where a set ships the same boxes several ways, it names the format on screen and switches between them on a keypress. items.summary: Overview This repository contains the replication data, source code, execution logs, and complete analytical outputs for the study: “Detectability of controlled leaks in an Andean water transmission main: a field evaluation of changepoint methods on flow and pressure signals.” The study evaluates the detectability of short-duration controlled leaks using five changepoint and anomaly-detection approaches applied to 30-second flow and pressure measurements collected during two field campaigns in an operational water transmission main in Loja, Ecuador. The evaluated methods are: Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Bayesian Information Criterion (PELT-BIC), Pruned Exact Linear Time using the Akaike Information Criterion (PELT-AIC), Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (BOCD), Cumulative Sum control charts (CUSUM), Moving-average ±3σ control-chart baseline. The repository contains the complete workflow used to: verify field records and ground-truth leak timings; perform campaign-specific spectral analyses using multitaper estimation; evaluate changepoint-detection performance; quantify event-level leak detectability; compare observed performance against chance-level expectations; assess BOCD sensitivity to hazard-rate and threshold settings; generate precision-recall curves and average-precision statistics; perform cross-campaign validation analyses; estimate theoretical detection-delay bounds for flow-based detection. This version supersedes earlier releases by correcting changepoint-index alignment, revising false-alarm-rate calculations using exposure time outside detection windows, replacing pooled spectral analyses with campaign-specific multitaper analyses, and incorporating event-level detectability, chance-level benchmarking, precision-recall evaluation, cross-campaign validation, and theoretical detection-delay analyses. items.summary: Motivation: Variant calling for next-generation sequencing (NGS) data relies on a diverse ecosystem of tools and workflows. Large-scale collaborative studies increasingly adopt federated analysis, where each institution processes sensitive data locally using standardized pipelines. Deploying identical pipelines across multiple centers remains challenging because heterogeneous software environments and computing policies can cause workflow divergence and inconsistent results. Results: We developed CBIcall, a workflow backend-flexible, configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling pipelines from raw FASTQ files to analysis-ready VCFs. Users define each analysis in a single YAML parameters file, which CBIcall resolves against a controlled workflow registry and resource catalog. The execution driver validates parameters and checks compatibility among pipelines, analysis modes, workflow backends, genome builds, tool versions, and resource bundles. CBIcall supports reproducibility auditing by comparing executions using recorded provenance and output fingerprints. CBIcall dispatches validated workflows natively through Bash, Cromwell, Nextflow and Snakemake backends and provides production-ready pipelines for germline WES, WGS (single-sample or cohort joint genotyping following GATK Best Practices), and mitochondrial DNA analysis. We evaluated analytical performance using public benchmark datasets and validated reproducibility across four computing environments. We further deployed CBIcall in the EU HEREDITARY project, where it processed 1102 samples with both WES and mtDNA pipelines on an institutional HPC system, supporting its suitability for reproducible cohort-scale genomic analyses. Availability and implementation: CBIcall is open source (GPLv3) and distributed with ready-to-run pipelines; full dependency and installation documentation is available at https://github.com/CNAG-Biomedical-Informatics/cbicall.
items.title: CBIcall: a configuration-driven framework for variant calling in large sequencing cohorts

items.summary: Despite significant advances in deep learning-based failure prognosis, existing predictive maintenance frameworks consistently terminate at the prediction step, leaving the critical operational challenge of prioritising maintenance resources across heterogeneous asset fleets unresolved. This paper addresses this gap by proposing an integrated framework that couples Long Short-Term Memory network-based Remaining Useful Life prediction with the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution for data-driven multi-criteria maintenance scheduling, validated on the NASA C-MAPSS FD001 turbofan degradation benchmark. The framework dynamically synthesises predicted health indicators with operational criteria encompassing machine criticality, maintenance cost, and production downtime impact to generate a ranked intervention schedule whose quality is evaluated through a rigorous, assumption-free protocol comprising precision-recall analysis, area under the precision-recall curve, Spearman rank correlation, and a scheduling efficiency ratio against a random baseline. A five-seed ablation study comparing Long Short-Term Memory, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory, and Gated Recurrent Unit architectures, with Wilcoxon signed-rank validation, establishes statistically equivalent prediction accuracy, confirming the architecture-agnostic nature of the scheduling design.
items.title: Code and analysis: A Deep Learning and TOPSIS Framework for Predictive Maintenance Scheduling in Smart Manufacturing: An Industry 4.0 Approach

items.summary: This record contains the replication data and R code for the study “How much does the publication universe matter? Source discontinuities and panel selection in OpenAlex” by Vladislav Bína and Jiří Přibil. The package includes OpenAlex source-by-year counts for 2010–2025 retrieved on 10–11 October 2026, supplementary OpenAlex and Crossref aggregate counts retrieved on 23 October 2026, a provenance-limited earlier archive of annual totals, and twelve annotated illustrative record checks. It also provides eight R scripts, expected numerical results, numerical inputs to the figures, and English documentation. The default workflow reproduces the saved-data analyses offline using base R. It covers publication growth, continuity panels, source turnover, panel-selection timing, population layers, and sensitivity to comparison horizons and endpoints. Version 2.2 was tested with R 4.5.2 on Windows. Data provenance, variable definitions, limitations and reproduction instructions are documented in README.md.
